learn.summary: A light-emitting diode (LED) gives light when current flows from the anode to the cathode.
tips: Always use a series resistor. Without one, the current gets too high and the LED fails.
The longer leg is the anode (+). The flat edge of the rim marks the cathode (−).
A red LED drops about 2 V. A typical current is 10 to 20 mA.
